notes.4: For this exercise, candidates were required to read a more extended text in which Christophe wrote about his experience of finding and returning a stray dog. The text was mostly straightforward, and the vocabulary covered familiar topics. Overall, candidates performed well on this exercise. The text was written in the first person, and the questions used the third person. Most questions could be answered by lifting a small number of words from the text, but the answers to Questions 4(f) and 4(k) required a minor manipulation to gain the mark. If candidates chose to lift more than was required to answer the other questions, they had to make any manipulation needed in the extra material, usually involving going from the first to the third person. It is generally advised to answer with the minimum number of words. Some candidates invalidated their answer to 4(b) by adding et vraiment mignon , which is information that does not answer the question. In 4(c) , candidates who added extra material in their answer did not make the necessary manipulation from moi to lui . Some candidates misunderstood 4(f) and 4(h) and answered with a different part of the text. In 4(i) , some candidates thought that Christophe wanted to take the dog to the vet’s and some responses to 4(j) suggested that the vet was holding the puce électronique . For 4(k) , some candidates did not make the necessary manipulation from mon chien to son chien and could not gain the mark. Cambridge International General Certificate of Secondary Education 0520 French November 2021
notes.5: In this exercise, candidates had to match a series of descriptions with statements from five people looking for a house. This exercise is aimed at the higher grades and the texts need to be read more closely in order to find the option that suits best. Each person’s statement gave quite specific requirements for the sort of house that they were looking for, and these details excluded all answers except the correct one. The statements included factors such as location, garden, size and need for restoration. Candidates need to ensure they consider all the information given as this is not a gist comprehension question. Description 7 was a frequent incorrect answer for 5(e) .
notes.6: This final exercise about volunteering was intended to be the most challenging part of the paper. About half the questions can be answered with a careful lift from the text and the others need a small manipulation of the text to answer the question. Very few candidates achieved full marks, and the questions seem to have discriminated appropriately. Although verbs do not necessarily have to be correct to score a mark, the tense usually must be appropriate to the question. Some candidates chose to paraphrase the text rather than lift words from the text. There is no need to do this, and although some candidates did this well, others used inappropriate synonyms when paraphrasing and could not gain the mark. In 6(a) , some candidates invalidated their answer by adding de transition . Sometimes, candidates answered questions in the wrong tense, particularly in 6(b) and 6(d) . For 6(h) and 6(i) , candidates often answered in the first person. Cambridge International General Certificate of Secondary Education 0520 French November 2021
